title: Top-down design: from requirements to functions
goal: Split an order calculation into parts with explicit intermediate values.

prerequisites.text: You know integer variables, multiplication, division and statement order.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: Task: three items at 100, with a 10 percent discount. First compute the subtotal, then the discount amount, then the total. Decomposition splits a task into steps, each answering one question.

subtotal is the amount before discount; saving is what we subtract; total is what we pay. Compute percent as subtotal*discount/100. Here 300*10/100 is exactly 30. Integer division discards the fractional part: agree on this rounding rule beforehand.

Use price and quantity 0..1000 and discount 0..100: the intermediate product is at most 100000000 and fits a 32-bit int. The example satisfies these bounds; handling arbitrary input is a later step. We do not need user-defined functions before learning how they work.

sections.title: Split an order calculation into parts with explicit intermediate values.
trace: Computed the amount to subtract, not the final total.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: At 100 percent, the entire subtotal is subtracted.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: Printing saving instead of total gives 30 rather than 270: a subtask was solved, but the wrong result was selected.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Calculate two items at 80 with a 25 percent discount. Print subtotal, saving and total separately and explain each number.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? Set discount=0, then discount=100.
selfcheck.feedback: At 0 percent, saving is 0. At 100 percent, the entire subtotal is subtracted.

selfcheck.prompt: Calculate two items at 80 with a 25 percent discount. Print subtotal, saving and total separately and explain each number.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. For price=80, count=2 and discount=25, subtotal=160, saving=40 and total=120. The saving of 40 must not be reported as the final cost of 120.

terms.definition: Breaking a large problem into smaller problems with explicit boundaries.
A named operation that receives arguments and can return a result.
The expected inputs, outputs and valid calling conditions.
